page: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-300s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation. Local storage is provided via a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. The server exhibits notable efficiency in text and image processing, both scoring in the top 25% tier. In language model tasks, text generation using a small 135M model achieves top-tier performance at 347.96 tokens per second, while text generation with a medium 7B model registers strong performance at 28.11 tokens per second. Memory bandwidth and database operations, such as Redis SET and Passmark database tests, consistently perform at average levels.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a cost-effective profile for compute-bound workloads that require dedicated CPU resources without the overhead of a high memory-to-core ratio. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly suitable for parallel processing tasks, software compilation, medium-scale web serving, and localized machine learning inference. It is also well-suited for applications requiring fast local storage access, such as transactional databases and text-processing pipelines, though workloads requiring massive memory footprints may find the 32.0 GB capacity a limiting factor.
